steps.tip: Mint's own Driver Manager (in the menu) does the same, with a choice of versions.

sections.heading: NVIDIA on Fedora
steps: Run "Install the NVIDIA driver (Fedora)". It adds RPM Fusion and installs the driver, which then builds itself (about 5 minutes).

steps.t: If Secure Boot is on, the results say so. Restart.
steps.see: A blue screen, Perform MOK management. Choose Enroll MOK, then Continue, Yes, type the password you were given, and Reboot.
steps.warn: If you skip this screen, the NVIDIA driver will not load. Run the command again to get another chance.

sections.heading: Broadcom Wi-Fi
steps: Connect the computer to the internet another way: a network cable, or a phone shared over USB (on the phone, turn on USB tethering).
Run "Install the Broadcom Wi-Fi driver", then restart. Wi-Fi networks appear in the network menu.

sections.heading: Firmware
steps: "Install missing firmware" installs the firmware package most Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and graphics chips need. On Debian, turn on the non-free-firmware component first.

title: Repairing a Linux system that will not start
summary: Using a Linux live USB and MendKit to check the drive and rebuild the startup menu and startup files.
need: A Linux live USB stick
Internet on the broken computer

sections.heading: Try these first

steps.t: At power-on, hold Shift (or tap Esc on newer systems) to show the GRUB startup menu. Choose Advanced options and an older kernel.
steps.tip: If that works, the newest kernel is the problem: update again later, or run "Always show the startup menu" so the older one is always one key away.

steps: Stuck at a black screen or "emergency mode" after an update: restore a Timeshift snapshot, or use the steps below with "Rebuild the startup files".

sections.heading: Start from a live USB
steps: Make a Ubuntu or Linux Mint USB stick (ISO Library and Rufus or Ventoy). It does not have to match the installed Linux.
Start the broken computer from it and choose Try or Start Linux Mint, not Install.
Connect to the internet (needed for Fedora, and to download MendKit).
Download the MendKit AppImage from the website. Open Terminal and type: sudo apt install libfuse2t64 (on 22.04: libfuse2). Then make the AppImage runnable and open it.

sections.heading: Repair with MendKit

steps.t: Tick Technician mode, open Repair, and click Open beside Repair a system that will not start.
steps.see: The partitions found, and notices for encrypted or LVM drives.

steps: Encrypted drive: open the Files app, click the encrypted drive and type its password, then reopen the screen. LVM: click Look for LVM partitions.

steps.t: Choose the installed system's partition, usually the largest ext4 or btrfs one.
steps.tip: MendKit checks it really holds an installed Linux before changing anything.

steps: Leave "Check and repair the file system" and "Reinstall and rebuild the startup menu" ticked. Tick "Rebuild the startup files" too if it stopped at a black screen or emergency mode.

steps.t: Click Repair it and type the live system's password if asked (often none: just press Enter).
steps.see: Results for the file system check and for the startup repair, naming the installed system.

steps: Shut down, remove the USB stick and start the computer.

sections.heading: If it still will not start
steps: The drive itself may be failing: check it with smartmontools from the live session, and copy the files off with MendKit's "Copy from an old drive".
Windows updates sometimes take over the startup order on dual-boot computers: in the computer's startup menu (F12 and similar), choose the Linux entry (ubuntu, Mint or Fedora).

title: Upgrading Linux to the next version
summary: Moving Ubuntu, Linux Mint or Fedora to its next release safely.

sections.heading: When
steps: MendKit's Dashboard warns when a version is close to or past the end of its security updates.
Ubuntu LTS and Linux Mint versions get 5 years of updates; Fedora about 13 months, so Fedora needs upgrading every year.

sections.heading: Get ready

steps.t: Open Repair and click Open beside Upgrade to the next version.
steps.see: Checks: free space (15 GB needed), mains power, waiting updates, a Timeshift snapshot, extra software sources, and the end of support date.

steps: Fix anything red. Install waiting updates in the Updates screen and restart.

steps.t: Take a Timeshift snapshot and back up personal files.
steps.warn: Upgrades usually go smoothly, but a power cut or a full drive mid-way can leave the computer unable to start.

sections.heading: Ubuntu and Linux Mint

steps.t: Click Start the upgrade.
steps.see: Ubuntu: the Software Updater offers the new version; click Upgrade. Mint: the Mint upgrade tool opens.

steps: Follow its screens. It asks for your password, checks again, downloads (30 to 90 minutes) and asks before replacing settings files: keep the current version unless you know otherwise.
Restart when it finishes. Extra software sources were turned off: turn them back on in Software & Updates (or Software Sources on Mint) if needed.

steps.t: Click Download Fedora N.
steps.see: MendKit installs current updates, then downloads the new release. The results list any package in the way.

steps.t: Save your work, then click Restart and upgrade.
steps.see: The computer restarts into an upgrade screen with a progress bar (30 to 60 minutes) and restarts again into the new Fedora.

title: Everyday Linux fixes
summary: Quick fixes for the problems Linux users run into most, and which MendKit recipe or command does each.

sections.heading: Desktop frozen or panel gone
steps: Dashboard: "The desktop froze or the panel vanished". It restarts Cinnamon, KDE Plasma, XFCE or MATE without closing your windows.
GNOME on Wayland cannot be restarted that way: sign out and back in. If nothing responds, press Ctrl, Alt and F3, sign in, and type: sudo systemctl restart gdm

sections.heading: Updates fail
steps: Recipe "Updates fail" handles "could not get lock" (waits for a running update, then finishes half-installed packages), broken extra sources (lists them; "Turn off broken software sources" sets them aside), held packages, Arch's expired signing keys and Snap updates.
Fedora: "Undo the last update (dnf)" rolls back an update that broke something.

sections.heading: No sound or wrong output
steps: Recipe "No sound" restarts the sound system, then "Reset the sound system completely" clears saved device choices. Afterwards, choose the output in Sound settings.

sections.heading: Printer or scanner
steps: Printers: "Install printer drivers" and "Install HP printer drivers". Most network printers work without a driver: "Printers on the network" lists them.
Scanners: Dashboard "The scanner does not work" installs scanner support, including network scanners.

sections.heading: Keeps asking to unlock the keyring
steps: Happens after a password change. Run "Keeps asking to unlock the keyring" (Repair) and sign out and in.

steps.t: Passwords saved in the old keyring (some apps and Chrome) must be typed again.
steps.warn: The old keyring is kept as a backup, but it needs the old password to open.

sections.heading: Screen problems
steps: Screen sharing or remote support shows black, or an older app misbehaves: try the X11 session (cog on the sign-in screen), or "Use X11 instead of Wayland (GNOME)".
Tearing lines in videos on XFCE: the "Stop screen tearing" tweak. On other desktops, try the Wayland session.
Text too small: the "Larger text" tweak for your desktop.

sections.heading: Slow to start
steps: Dashboard "It takes ages to start" shows which services hold startup up. NetworkManager-wait-online is the usual culprit on desktops; turn it off in Startup items.

sections.heading: Out of space
steps: Repair, Free up space: caches, downloaded update files, old logs, old kernels, old Snap versions, unused Flatpak parts, Docker and Timeshift snapshots, and large files to look at.

title: Securing a Linux computer
summary: Checking and fixing the firewall, automatic updates, remote login and remote access programs.

steps.t: Run the recipe "Linux security checkup".
steps.see: Firewall, automatic security updates, remote login (SSH), who has administrator rights, disk encryption and which programs accept network connections.

sections.heading: Fix

steps.t: Run "Secure this computer". It turns on the firewall (blocking incoming connections only) and automatic security updates.
steps.tip: If remote login (SSH) is in use, MendKit keeps it allowed through the firewall.

steps: If SSH is on and nobody logs in remotely, turn it off: sudo systemctl disable --now ssh
Check the administrators listed are people who should have that power.

sections.heading: Remote access programs
steps: Check for remote access (Dashboard) now removes AnyDesk, TeamViewer, RustDesk and others on Linux too: it stops their services, uninstalls the package or Flatpak and sets loose copies aside.

sections.heading: Encryption
steps: Disk encryption can only be turned on by reinstalling, with "Encrypt the new Linux installation" ticked in the installer. Worth it for laptops.

title: 7-Zip
summary: Opens and makes zip, 7z, rar and other compressed files.

sections.heading: What it is
steps: 7-Zip opens almost any compressed file (zip, 7z, rar, tar, iso) and can make zip or 7z files, with a password if wanted.

sections.heading: When to use it
steps: A download ends in .7z or .rar and Windows cannot open it.
Packing a folder into one file to email or copy.

sections.heading: Install it

steps.t: Open MendKit. At the bottom left, tick Technician mode.
steps.see: Repair, Tools and Tweaks appear in the menu on the left.

steps.t: Click Tools in the menu. Type 7-Zip in the search box at the top, or scroll to find it.
steps.see: A row for 7-Zip with a tick box, its job, its licence and a Status column.

steps.t: Tick the box beside 7-Zip and click Install selected.
steps.see: The bottom panel shows the download and install. It usually takes one to five minutes.
steps.tip: On Windows, use "Restart as administrator" on the Dashboard first so installs do not stop to ask permission. On a Mac or Linux, MendKit asks for your password once.

steps.t: Wait until the Status column says Installed.
steps.tip: If it says it failed, check the internet connection and click Install selected again. The full reason is in Reports.

steps.t: Click the Start button (the Windows logo at the bottom of the screen), type 7-Zip and click it in the list.
steps.see: 7-Zip opens in its own window. If Windows asks "Do you want to allow this app to make changes to your device?", click Yes.

steps: 7-Zip has no window of its own: it runs in Terminal (Command Prompt or PowerShell on Windows). See the guide "Opening Terminal and typing a command" if you have not done this before.

sections.heading: How to use it

steps.t: Windows: right-click the compressed file, choose Show more options, then 7-Zip, then Extract to "folder name\".
steps.see: A new folder beside the file with its contents.

steps: To make one: right-click a file or folder, Show more options, 7-Zip, Add to "name.zip".
On a Mac and Linux, 7-Zip is a Terminal command: 7zz x file.7z (Mac) or 7z x file.7z (Linux) extracts into the current folder.

sections.heading: If something goes wrong
steps: "Wrong password" or "Data error": the file is incomplete or damaged. Download it again.

sections.heading: Take care
steps: Compressed files from unknown senders can hide malware. Scan them first.

title: AdwCleaner
summary: Removes adware, browser hijackers and pushy "optimiser" programs.

sections.heading: What it is
steps: AdwCleaner is a small Malwarebytes tool aimed at adware: toolbars, changed home pages and search engines, and unwanted browser add-ons. It runs without installing anything else.

sections.heading: When to use it
steps: The browser's home page or search engine keeps changing.
Ads appear where they should not.

steps.t: Open MendKit. At the bottom left, tick Technician mode.
steps.see: Repair, Tools and Tweaks appear in the menu on the left.

steps.t: Click Tools in the menu. Type AdwCleaner in the search box at the top, or scroll to find it.
steps.see: A row for AdwCleaner with a tick box, its job, its licence and a Status column.

steps.t: Tick the box beside AdwCleaner and click Install selected.
steps.see: The bottom panel shows the download and install. It usually takes one to five minutes.
steps.tip: On Windows, use "Restart as administrator" on the Dashboard first so installs do not stop to ask permission. On a Mac or Linux, MendKit asks for your password once.

steps.t: Wait until the Status column says Installed.
steps.tip: If it says it failed, check the internet connection and click Install selected again. The full reason is in Reports.

steps.t: Click the Start button (the Windows logo at the bottom of the screen), type AdwCleaner and click it in the list.
steps.see: AdwCleaner opens in its own window. If Windows asks "Do you want to allow this app to make changes to your device?", click Yes.

sections.heading: How to use it

steps.t: Close all browsers. Open AdwCleaner and Agree to the terms.
steps.see: A dashboard with Scan now.

steps.t: Click Scan now.
steps.see: Usually under a minute. Then a list of findings grouped by type.

steps: Leave everything ticked unless it is a program the person wants, and click Quarantine.

steps.t: Click Continue at the warning: programs will be closed.
steps.see: A request to restart the computer.

steps: Restart. After restarting, a log opens showing what was removed.

sections.heading: Reading the results
steps: Items under Preinstalled software are things the computer maker added. Untick them if the person uses them.
Basic repair (under Settings) also resets browser policies and network settings; leave it at default unless the browser is still hijacked.

sections.heading: Take care
steps: AdwCleaner is free for personal use only. Using it on customers' computers as a business needs the paid licence from its maker.

title: Angry IP Scanner
summary: Quickly lists every device on the network with its name and address.

sections.heading: What it is
steps: Angry IP Scanner checks every address on the local network and lists the devices that answer, with their names and makers.

sections.heading: When to use it
steps: Finding a printer's address, or what is connected to the Wi-Fi.

steps.t: Open MendKit. At the bottom left, tick Technician mode.
steps.see: Repair, Tools and Tweaks appear in the menu on the left.

steps.t: Click Tools in the menu. Type Angry IP Scanner in the search box at the top, or scroll to find it.
steps.see: A row for Angry IP Scanner with a tick box, its job, its licence and a Status column.

steps.t: Tick the box beside Angry IP Scanner and click Install selected.
steps.see: The bottom panel shows the download and install. It usually takes one to five minutes.
steps.tip: On Windows, use "Restart as administrator" on the Dashboard first so installs do not stop to ask permission. On a Mac or Linux, MendKit asks for your password once.

steps.t: Wait until the Status column says Installed.
steps.tip: If it says it failed, check the internet connection and click Install selected again. The full reason is in Reports.

steps.t: Click the Start button (the Windows logo at the bottom of the screen), type Angry IP Scanner and click it in the list.
steps.see: Angry IP Scanner opens in its own window. If Windows asks "Do you want to allow this app to make changes to your device?", click Yes.

steps.t: Open Finder, click Applications in the left column and double-click Angry IP Scanner. Or press Command and Space together, type Angry IP Scanner and press Return.
steps.see: If macOS says Angry IP Scanner was downloaded from the internet, click Open.

sections.heading: How to use it

steps.t: Open Angry IP Scanner.
steps.see: IP Range with the network's range filled in, and a Start button.

steps.t: Click Start.
steps.see: Each address with a coloured dot: blue for devices that answered.

steps: Click Tools, Preferences, Display, and choose Alive hosts only to hide the empty ones.

sections.heading: Reading the results
steps: Hostname and MAC Vendor columns help identify each device (for example HP for a printer).

sections.heading: Take care
steps: Only scan networks you own or manage.

title: AppCleaner
summary: Removes Mac apps together with their leftover settings and caches.

sections.heading: What it is

sections.heading: When to use it

sections.heading: How to use it
steps: Quit the app you want to remove.

steps.t: Open AppCleaner.
steps.see: A window saying Drop your apps here.

steps.t: Drag the app from Applications onto the window.
steps.see: The app and its related files, all ticked.

steps: Click Remove and type your password if asked.

sections.heading: Take care
steps: The files go to the Trash. Empty it once you are sure.

You choose what to clean from a list, and it shows what it would delete before deleting anything.

sections.heading: When to use it

Clearing private browsing traces before passing a computer on.

steps.tip: If it says it failed, check the internet connection and click Install selected again. The full reason is in Reports.

steps.t: Click the Start button (the Windows logo at the bottom of the screen), type BleachBit and click it in the list.
steps.see: BleachBit opens in its own window. If Windows asks "Do you want to allow this app to make changes to your device?", click Yes.

steps: Open the applications menu (the grid of dots or the menu button in the corner), type BleachBit and click it.

steps.t: Close the browsers and other programs you want to clean.
steps.tip: BleachBit cannot clean a program that is open.

steps.t: Open BleachBit.
steps.see: The first time, a Preferences window. Close it. The main window has a list of programs on the left with tick boxes.

steps.t: Tick System, then Temporary files and Cache under it. Under each browser tick Cache. Leave Passwords, Form history and Cookies unticked unless the person wants to be signed out of everything.
steps.warn: Items marked in red or with a warning (such as Free disk space, or Memory) are slow or risky. Leave them unticked.

steps.t: Click Preview.
steps.see: The files that would be deleted and how much space would be freed. Nothing is deleted yet.

steps.t: If the list looks right, click Clean, then Delete to confirm.
steps.see: "Disk space recovered" with the amount.

sections.heading: Reading the results
steps: "Disk space recovered" is what was freed.
"Files deleted" counts the files removed. A few "permission denied" lines are normal for files in use.

sections.heading: If something goes wrong
steps: Nothing freed: the programs were open, or there was little junk.
Signed out of websites: Cookies was ticked. Sign in again.

sections.heading: Take care
steps: Do not tick "Free disk space" on an SSD; it is slow and wears the drive for no benefit.

steps: The same driver every time: update or remove that driver or the hardware it belongs to (for example nvlddmkm.sys is the NVIDIA graphics driver).

steps.tip: If it says it failed, check the internet connection and click Install selected again. The full reason is in Reports.

steps.t: Tick the programs to remove and click Uninstall (Uninstall quietly if offered).
steps.see: A confirmation listing what will be removed. Click Continue.

steps: Wait for the uninstallers. Some may show their own window; follow it.

steps.t: When it offers to look for leftovers, click Yes.
steps.see: A list of leftover folders and registry entries, each with a confidence level.

steps.t: Keep only items marked Very good or Good ticked and click Delete selected.

title: ClamAV
summary: A free virus scanner that checks files and folders for known malware.

sections.heading: What it is
steps: ClamAV is an open-source virus scanner. It has no window: you run a scan from Terminal and read the list it prints.
It is a second opinion, not a replacement for the built-in protection (Microsoft Defender on Windows, XProtect on a Mac).

sections.heading: When to use it
steps: A second scan when you suspect malware.
Checking a USB stick or a folder of downloads before opening it.
Linux computers, which have no built-in scanner.

sections.heading: Install it

steps.t: Open MendKit. At the bottom left, tick Technician mode.
steps.see: Repair, Tools and Tweaks appear in the menu on the left.

steps.tip: If it says it failed, check the internet connection and click Install selected again. The full reason is in Reports.

steps: ClamAV has no window of its own: it runs in Terminal (Command Prompt or PowerShell on Windows). See the guide "Opening Terminal and typing a command" if you have not done this before.

sections.heading: How to use it
steps: Open Terminal (see "Opening Terminal and typing a command"). On Windows, open it as administrator.

steps.t: Update the virus definitions first. Type freshclam and press Enter.
steps.see: "Downloading daily.cvd" and "database updated". It takes a minute or two.
steps.tip: Linux: sudo freshclam. Windows: if freshclam says the config file is missing, run MendKit's malware scan recipe once; it sets ClamAV up.

steps.t: Scan your user folder. Windows: clamscan -r -i %USERPROFILE%   Mac and Linux: clamscan -r -i ~
steps.see: Nothing for a while (it can take 30 minutes or more), then a SCAN SUMMARY.
steps.tip: -r means look in every folder inside; -i means only list infected files.

steps: Read the summary at the end.

sections.heading: Reading the results
steps: "Infected files: 0" means nothing known was found.
Each line ending FOUND names a file and the malware it matched, for example Downloads/setup.exe: Win.Trojan.Agent FOUND.
"Known viruses" is how many patterns it checked against.

sections.heading: If something goes wrong
steps: "command not found": the install did not finish; reinstall from Tools.
A FOUND file you trust (for example a password tool or crack-detection test file) can be a false alarm. Search the name it matched.

sections.heading: Take care
steps: ClamAV only reports. To remove a file it found, delete it yourself or quarantine it with Malwarebytes. Do not delete files in Windows or System folders.

steps: A drive clicks, is very slow, or shows read errors, and its files matter.

steps.t: Wait until the Status column says Installed.
steps.tip: If it says it failed, check the internet connection and click Install selected again. The full reason is in Reports.

steps: GNU ddrescue has no window of its own: it runs in Terminal (Command Prompt or PowerShell on Windows). See the guide "Opening Terminal and typing a command" if you have not done this before.

sections.heading: How to use it

steps.t: Connect the failing drive and a healthy drive at least as large.
steps.warn: Everything on the healthy (destination) drive will be overwritten. Getting the source and destination the wrong way round destroys the files you are trying to save.

steps.t: Find both drives. Linux: sudo lsblk -o NAME,SIZE,MODEL   Mac: diskutil list
steps.see: Each drive with its size and model, such as sdb 500G and sdc 1T (Linux) or disk2 and disk3 (Mac). Write down which is which.

steps: Unmount any volumes on them. Mac: diskutil unmountDisk /dev/disk2 (for each). Linux: they are not mounted if nothing opened them.

steps.t: First pass, fast, skipping bad areas. Linux: sudo ddrescue -n /dev/sdb /dev/sdc rescue.map   Mac: sudo ddrescue -n /dev/rdisk2 /dev/rdisk3 rescue.map
steps.see: A live status: rescued, bad areas, read errors and the time remaining.
steps.tip: First the failing drive, then the healthy one, then the log file name. The -f option may be needed to write to a whole drive: add -f before -n.

steps: Second pass, retrying bad areas three times: same command with -r3 instead of -n.
When finished, run TestDisk, PhotoRec, or MendKit's "Copy from an old drive" on the healthy copy, never on the failing drive.

sections.heading: Reading the results
steps: "pct rescued" near 100% is a near-complete copy. Bad areas show how much could not be read.
The rescue.map file lets you stop with Ctrl C and run the same command later to continue.

sections.heading: Take care
steps: If a drive makes clicking or grinding noises, every hour running can make it worse. For irreplaceable files, a professional lab is the safest choice.

steps: Open Terminal as administrator (Windows), or a normal Terminal on a Mac or Linux.

summary: Updates all the apps on a Windows computer from one window.

sections.heading: What it is
steps: UniGetUI is a friendly window on top of winget and other Windows package managers. It shows which apps have updates and installs them together.

sections.heading: When to use it
steps: Bringing every app up to date after a repair.
Finding and installing common free programs.

steps.t: Open MendKit. At the bottom left, tick Technician mode.
steps.see: Repair, Tools and Tweaks appear in the menu on the left.

steps.t: Click Tools in the menu. Type UniGetUI in the search box at the top, or scroll to find it.
steps.see: A row for UniGetUI with a tick box, its job, its licence and a Status column.

steps.t: Tick the box beside UniGetUI and click Install selected.
steps.see: The bottom panel shows the download and install. It usually takes one to five minutes.
steps.tip: On Windows, use "Restart as administrator" on the Dashboard first so installs do not stop to ask permission. On a Mac or Linux, MendKit asks for your password once.

steps.t: Wait until the Status column says Installed.
steps.tip: If it says it failed, check the internet connection and click Install selected again. The full reason is in Reports.

steps.t: Click the Start button (the Windows logo at the bottom of the screen), type UniGetUI and click it in the list.
steps.see: UniGetUI opens in its own window. If Windows asks "Do you want to allow this app to make changes to your device?", click Yes.

sections.heading: How to use it

steps.t: Open UniGetUI.
steps.see: A list of sections on the left: Discover packages, Software updates, Installed packages.

steps.t: Click Software updates.
steps.see: Each app with an update, its current version and the new one.

steps.t: Tick the apps to update (or all) and click Update selected packages.
steps.see: Progress for each app. Some may show their own installer window.

steps: Restart the computer if asked.

sections.heading: Reading the results
steps: Apps that updated leave the list. Failed ones show a red mark; click it for the reason.

sections.heading: If something goes wrong
steps: An app that keeps failing: close the app first, or update it from its own Help menu.

title: Ventoy
summary: Makes one USB stick that can start many different ISO files: installers and rescue systems.
need: A USB stick of 32 GB or more

sections.heading: What it is

sections.heading: When to use it
steps: Building a technician USB with Windows installers, Memtest86+, Hiren's and Linux rescue systems on one stick.

steps.t: Open MendKit. At the bottom left, tick Technician mode.
steps.see: Repair, Tools and Tweaks appear in the menu on the left.

steps.t: Click Tools in the menu. Type Ventoy in the search box at the top, or scroll to find it.
steps.see: A row for Ventoy with a tick box, its job, its licence and a Status column.

steps.t: Tick the box beside Ventoy and click Install selected.
steps.see: The bottom panel shows the download and install. It usually takes one to five minutes.
steps.tip: On Windows, use "Restart as administrator" on the Dashboard first so installs do not stop to ask permission. On a Mac or Linux, MendKit asks for your password once.

steps.t: Wait until the Status column says Installed.

sections.heading: How to use it

steps.t: Plug in the USB stick.
steps.warn: Installing Ventoy erases everything on the stick.

steps.t: Open Ventoy2Disk (click Start and type Ventoy). Click Yes when Windows asks.
steps.see: A window with Device (the stick), the Ventoy version in package and on the device, and Install and Update buttons.

steps.t: Check the Device box shows your USB stick: its size and name. Read it twice.
steps.warn: If more than one drive is listed, the wrong choice erases that drive instead.

steps.t: Click Install, then Yes to both warnings.
steps.see: "Congratulations! Ventoy has been successfully installed to the device." The stick now shows as a drive called Ventoy.

steps: Copy ISO files onto the Ventoy drive in File Explorer, like any other files. Folders are fine.
Eject the stick. To use it, start the computer from it (see "Starting a computer from a USB stick") and pick an ISO from the menu.

sections.heading: Reading the results
steps: To update Ventoy later, click Update instead of Install: files on the stick are kept.

sections.heading: If something goes wrong
steps: Ventoy menu says the image is not supported, or it freezes: choose the ISO, then press Enter on "Boot in grub2 mode" or "WIMBOOT mode".
Secure Boot error: on first boot, choose Enroll key from disk, ENROLL_THIS_KEY_IN_MOKMANAGER.cer, Continue, Yes and Reboot.

sections.heading: When to use it

Finding forgotten large files: old videos, game installers, backups.

sections.heading: How to use it

steps.t: Open WinDirStat.
steps.see: A box asking which drives to scan.

steps.t: Choose the C: drive (or All Local Drives) and click OK.
steps.see: Pac-Man icons while it scans, which can take a few minutes. Then a folder list at the top and the colour map below.

steps: Click the arrow beside the biggest folders in the list to open them, largest first.
Click a large rectangle in the map to find which file it is.

steps.t: To delete something, right-click it and choose Delete (to Recycle Bin).
steps.warn: Do not delete anything inside Windows, Program Files, ProgramData or AppData unless you know what it is. Uninstall programs the normal way instead.

sections.heading: Reading the results
steps: Huge pagefile.sys and hiberfil.sys files belong to Windows and are normal.
A large folder under Users is personal files: ask before deleting.
Windows.old (after an upgrade) can be removed with Disk Cleanup, Clean up system files.

title: Wireshark
summary: Captures and shows network traffic packet by packet.

sections.heading: What it is
steps: Wireshark records the network traffic passing through a computer and shows every message. A specialist tool for network problems.

sections.heading: When to use it
steps: Deep network troubleshooting, when simpler checks have not found the problem.

sections.heading: Install it

steps.t: Open MendKit. At the bottom left, tick Technician mode.
steps.see: Repair, Tools and Tweaks appear in the menu on the left.

steps.t: Click Tools in the menu. Type Wireshark in the search box at the top, or scroll to find it.
steps.see: A row for Wireshark with a tick box, its job, its licence and a Status column.

steps.see: The bottom panel shows the download and install. It usually takes one to five minutes.
steps.tip: On Windows, use "Restart as administrator" on the Dashboard first so installs do not stop to ask permission. On a Mac or Linux, MendKit asks for your password once.

steps.t: Wait until the Status column says Installed.
steps.tip: If it says it failed, check the internet connection and click Install selected again. The full reason is in Reports.

steps.see: Wireshark opens in its own window. If Windows asks "Do you want to allow this app to make changes to your device?", click Yes.

steps.t: Open Finder, click Applications in the left column and double-click Wireshark. Or press Command and Space together, type Wireshark and press Return.
steps.see: If macOS says Wireshark was downloaded from the internet, click Open.

steps: Open the applications menu (the grid of dots or the menu button in the corner), type Wireshark and click it.

sections.heading: How to use it

steps.t: Open Wireshark.
steps.see: A list of network interfaces with small live activity graphs.

steps.t: Double-click the interface with activity (Wi-Fi or Ethernet).
steps.see: Packets scrolling past.

steps: Reproduce the problem, then click the red square to stop.
Type a filter in the bar at the top and press Enter, for example dns, or ip.addr == 192.168.1.1.
File, Save As to keep the capture for a technician.

sections.heading: Reading the results
steps: Red or black rows are errors such as retransmissions or resets.

sections.heading: Take care
steps: Captures can contain private information. Only capture on networks you own, and share files only with someone you trust.
